hits.text: ## Pitch and player promise

A new apprentice, Isaac, arrives at the failing lighthouse on Bracken Isle. Keeper Ted opens the door to “the new guy” and, after a beat, sends him down to the basement to shovel coal into the boiler. Overwhelmed by the storm, two sailors, Arthur and Daniel, moor their rowboat at the island’s dock and look for shelter; Ted sees them from the window and tells the apprentice to open the island gate.

## Scope and release target

Full game, about 30 minutes: three compact locations, the arrival and lighthouse work (feeding the boiler, then further repairs), the sailors’ arrival and the island gate, Ted’s discovery of the broken burner, two crossings with Arthur, a final repair under the running ship deadline, win and fail outcomes, optional discoveries, and controller support. The sea has a state from 0 to 5: the first crossing is easy (1 to 2) and the return is hectic (3 to 5), with both docks sheltered. Status: input to Decisions to be made item 8 (engine), 25 September 2026. Compares Godot, Unity and Unreal for this project, then contrasts all three with Phaser. Licence terms change; check each vendor’s current terms before committing.
• PC release on Steam, with controller support in the full game.
• Free and MIT-licensed: no royalties, fees, or revenue thresholds.
• Small, fast editor; quick to open, iterate, and export. Runs well on modest hardware.
• Console ports need third-party porting services (not relevant for a PC-first release).
• Runs in any browser, which makes it trivial to share builds with playtesters (for example on itch.io).
• Steam release needs a desktop wrapper (Electron, NW.js, or Tauri), plus extra work for Steamworks and controller support.
• Only as a throwaway 2D steering sketch to test hazard layouts in a day or two, or if the game pivoted to a 2D web release.
|Cost and licence               |Free, MIT                 |Free below revenue threshold   |Free, royalty above high threshold|Free, MIT                      |

A shippable prototype here means a 10-minute greybox build you can hand to playtesters (for example through itch.io or a Steam Playtest), passing the prototype outcome checks in the Executive Summary. It is not a product to sell.
A shippable full game means a 30-minute commercial Steam release with final art, audio, accessibility, and a store page. Estimated solo effort:
|Steam integration, store page, trailer, capsule art         |2      |

That is about 6–7 months solo. Buying stock asset packs for environments and characters, and using AI voice, could bring it to about 5 months. Steam also requires a public Coming Soon store page for at least two weeks before launch, plus review time for the store page and build, so plan the store page well before the end.
